answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after a random peer challenges them to solve a fresh task, then stakes tokens that are slashed if later audits find copied or coordinated answers. The challenge changes each round, so one operator cannot cheaply replay a single response across many identities; those identities must each spend time and lock capital. A prism prompt can expose an echo farm, while audits on a knoll of unusually similar agents make the attacker risk losing the stake.
